candidate.change: The three sim-v1 minutes classifiers (P(start), P(60+|start), P(cameo)) receive 7 extra inputs, all from the obs_ variant only: obs_mins_7d, obs_mins_14d, obs_starts_7d, obs_starts_14d, obs_apps_14d, obs_euro_mins_14d, obs_rest_days (NULL is kept as missing; HistGradientBoosting handles it natively). It also receives the flags linked and obs_link_suspect. Nothing else changes: the availability overlay, horizon decay, scoring rules, seed and hyperparameters stay the same.

baseline: sim-v1 minutes classifiers as on master 51f0def, with features MINUTES_FEATURES, the same training rows and the same seed.
training_data_rule: VALIDATED variant (the only one that can support promotion): the candidate's extra inputs are obs_ values computed at each training row's own cutoff, and training rows come only from eligible gameweeks before the evaluated gameweek. The baseline is trained on exactly the same rows. Each evaluated gameweek must also satisfy the repair condition: the source has repair_log, and the obs_ rows rewritten after the cutoff are excluded (workload.py repair_proof). Otherwise that gameweek is not usable. EXPLORATORY variant, declared now and never counted as validated: train on rec_ values from earlier or reconstructed history and evaluate on obs_. Training/serving skew is possible; results are reported only as exploratory. No other mixture is allowed.
evaluation_rows: Every player in the observed bootstrap pull that eligibility.gameweek uses, for each eligible gameweek, with excluded matches removed (db-eligibility). Targets: official FPL minutes in that gameweek's fixture(s). Players in a double gameweek count once per fixture. Each gameweek must be eligible AND have repair_proof starting 'repair_log present'.
paired_unit: The same player-fixture rows, cutoff, targets and exclusions for baseline and candidate.
cohorts: link-suspect players (obs_link_suspect: other-club rows only, workload NULL)
secondary_metrics: Brier score of P(start) and P(60+)
calibration intercept and slope of P(start)

points_metrics.purpose: Gate so a minutes-model gain cannot be presented as a points gain without evidence.
points_metrics.unit: One row per (player, eligible gameweek): predicted = sim expected FPL points for that gameweek (sum over its fixtures, proj xpts); actual = official total_points from fpl_points_gw summed over the gameweek. Same unit and row filter as model/backtest.projection_backtest(validated=True), including dropping player-gameweeks that touch an excluded match.
points_metrics.pairing: Baseline sim-v1 and candidate sim-v1-workload on exactly the same rows, cutoffs, SimConfig samples, seed and refit schedule (refit_every=6). Rows missing on either side are counted and reported (as backtest.paired_comparison does), never silently dropped.
points_metrics.metric: RMSE of xP vs actual points (primary); MAE and bias reported.
cohorts: decision-relevant: baseline xP >= 2.0 (defined by the baseline only)
the r2 cohorts (trusted linked, unlinked, link-suspect, euro_mins_14d > 0, rest_days < 4)
points_metrics.uncertainty: Paired bootstrap of the RMSE difference (candidate - baseline), resampling players within each gameweek, 2000 draws, seed 20261030; 95% interval reported with every number.
points_metrics.points_improvement_claim_bar: All of: paired RMSE reduction >= 1% on all rows; upper bound of the bootstrap 95% interval of the difference < 0; decision-relevant cohort does not regress (ratio <= 1.0); same sign in at least 2 of 3 or more gameweeks, leaving one gameweek out at a time.
points_metrics.implementation_note: Reuse backtest.projection_backtest(validated=True) once per model with the minutes model injected, then the paired_comparison logic with the candidate in place of a baseline. No code is written until the run is authorised.

team_points_report.role: REPORTED ONLY. Never a gate, never evidence of a points gain.
team_points_report.policy: model/replay.replay_season(validated=True) run once per model with identical ReplayConfig defaults (horizon, samples, seed, solver settings), the same starting squad (the real squad at the first evaluated deadline when known, else the same free first pick), the same chip rules and the same eligible gameweeks.
reported: actual points per gameweek and total, each run and the difference
team_points_report.why_not_a_gate: Weekly team score SD is about 15-20 points; a plausible xP gain moves expected team points by well under 1 point a week, so over 3-10 gameweeks the result is noise.
team_points_report.label: descriptive; not evidence of a points gain

acceptance_rule: Promotion requires all of the following: every sample minimum passes; both primary metrics improve by at least 2% (paired, all rows); the calibration slope is within 0.8-1.2; no cohort with at least 300 rows regresses by more than 1% on either primary metric; the unlinked and link-suspect cohorts (workload NULL) must each regress by no more than 1% on either primary metric whatever their size, and are reported even below 300 rows; and the improvement holds in a leave-one-gameweek-out check (sign is the same in at least 2 of 3 or more gameweeks). In addition, the points_metrics non_inferiority_gate must pass (all rows, decision-relevant cohort and every position cohort with at least 300 rows). Otherwise the candidate is labelled experimental or rejected. Synthetic checks and reconstructed history never count as performance evidence. No factor or hyperparameter tuning on the evaluated gameweeks.
claims_rule: Minutes metrics pass, points gate fails: 'improves minutes forecasts; no points benefit shown'. Not promoted.
Minutes metrics pass, points non-inferior: 'improves minutes forecasts without hurting points'. Promotion allowed if all other conditions hold.
Only if points_improvement_claim_bar passes may 'improves expected-points accuracy' be said.
Team-points replay results never support 'scored more points', whatever the sign.
Exploratory or reconstructed gameweeks support no claim.
earliest_possible_run: After the provenance patch (FAA-41, 6767d6d0) is merged and records fpl_deadlines before each deadline, at least 3 eligible gameweeks must exist (about GW12 if recording starts before the GW9 deadline). FotMob appearances must also keep being ingested before each cutoff; obs_ coverage is reported per gameweek by workload.py.
known_limits_declared_now: Domestic cups (FA Cup, EFL Cup) and international matches are not in the database, so workload is a lower bound, worst just after international breaks.
About 18% of FPL players have no FotMob link (NULL workload).
appearances.ingested_at is the time of the row's last write (INSERT OR REPLACE), so obs_ is conservative: rows rewritten after the cutoff drop out.
Name-based links merge namesakes. Rows for another club are dropped (153-187 rows per gameweek in GW6-8). A player with only other-club rows in 30 days is link-suspect (NULL), 60-69 per gameweek.
